clue.text: Sad secret disturbed philosopher

indicators.note: something disturbed has been knocked out of its settled order, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A troubled thinker is unsettled by some gloomy secret he keeps.
explanation.walkthrough: SAD SECRET rearranges into DESCARTES, the French thinker of 'I think, therefore I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes was a seventeenth-century French philosopher and mathematician.

clue.text: Odd editor gets up to object

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: rum is an old word for odd or strange
ED is the short form of editor

explanation.surface: A peculiar editor rises to raise an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise a doubt or protest, so it is a synonym for to object.

clue.text: Something funny about our dip

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the funny thing goes around the other word

blocks.note: a scream is something hilarious
taken as written

explanation.surface: There's something comical about the dip we brought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something funny' is a noun phrase here, the way a hilarious person is called a real scream.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour cream is a thick soured dairy product commonly served as a dip for chips.

clue.text: Giving up cook, bad at icing

indicators.note: to cook something is to work it into a new form, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A baker who is hopeless at decorating cakes quits the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' looks like the name of a job, but it is an imperative meaning rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdicating means renouncing a throne or responsibility, a form of giving up.

clue.text: Vilify a number of Romans breaking ceasefire

indicators.note: something breaking into a thing splits it open and sits inside

blocks.note: a truce is a ceasefire
taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Slander a group of Roman soldiers for violating an armistice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number of Romans' looks like a squad of soldiers, but it means one Roman numeral, joined to the article before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce someone is to speak badly of them and damage their reputation, much like vilify.

clue.text: Southern post office applies for partners

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
PO is the abbreviation for post office
to apply something is to use it

explanation.surface: A branch office in the south takes applications from couples.
explanation.definitionFit: Spouses are husbands and wives, each one the marital partner of the other.

clue.text: True Conservatives

blocks.note: first meaning: correct, accurate
second meaning: the political wing of conservatives, as opposed to the left

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a tribute to loyal party members, but the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means correct as an adjective and, as a noun, the conservative side of politics.

clue.text: Theme park attraction free before end of June

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: to rid is to free of something
the final letter of June

explanation.surface: An amusement park offers free entry to an attraction until late June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like no charge, but it is the verb meaning clear.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride, such as a rollercoaster, is a typical attraction at an amusement park.

clue.text: Immature bowlers here?

blocks.note: first meaning: inexperienced or unripe
second meaning: the lawn where bowls is played

explanation.walkthrough: Bowls is a lawn game in which players roll balls towards a small target, played on a closely cut green.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means naive or unripe, and is also the flat lawn on which the game of bowls is played.

clue.text: Elope then surprisingly produce ring

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is unexpected, so the letters come out in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A couple running off to marry unexpectedly results in an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a wedding band, but it is the verb meaning to call.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is British usage for calling them on the phone.

clue.text: Form of fungal growth

blocks.note: first meaning: a shape or cast into which material is poured
second meaning: the furry growth on old food

explanation.surface: It reads as a biology label: a particular type of fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' looks like 'a kind of', but Form is a definition on its own, joined to the second by 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mould is both a hollow shape for casting and a furry fungus that grows on damp or stale things.

clue.text: Lots of cards distributed satisfactorily?

blocks.note: first meaning: a large amount
second meaning, read literally: a hand of cards dealt well

explanation.surface: It sounds like many playing cards being handed out to everyone's satisfaction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal second reading: a satisfactory deal of the cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for plenty, and taken word by word it describes a fair round of dealing at the card table.

clue.text: Ethnicity lessons in Ascot, for example

blocks.note: race is a synonym for ethnicity
a course is a series of lessons

explanation.surface: A curriculum on ethnicity is being taught at Ascot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous English horse-racing venue in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is an example of a track where horse races are run.

clue.text: Game children might play in break

blocks.note: first meaning: a simple card game where matching cards are called out
second meaning: to crack or split suddenly

explanation.surface: Pupils playing a game during their school break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like playtime, but it is the verb meaning to crack.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a matching-cards game for children and also means to break sharply, as a twig does.

clue.text: Cleaners reveal a princess taken in by her husband

indicators.note: being taken in by someone means being held within them

blocks.note: Prince Charles was Princess Diana's husband
taken as written
Di was the popular name for Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: Domestic staff disclose that a royal princess was fooled by her own husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like deceived, but it means held inside; the husband is the then Prince of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Charladies are women employed to clean houses or offices, the same as cleaners.

clue.text: Cuts made here where players work?

blocks.note: first meaning: the hospital room where surgeons operate
second meaning: the building where actors perform

explanation.surface: It suggests a place where budget cuts hit a company of performers.
explanation.walkthrough: The operating theatre is the British term for a surgical room, where incisions are made.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the surgical operating room and the playhouse where actors perform.

clue.text: Kill artist in the highest social class

blocks.note: to top someone is slang for to kill them
a drawer is someone who draws

explanation.surface: An order to murder a painter from the upper crust.
explanation.walkthrough: Top drawer, literally the uppermost drawer in a chest, is an idiom for the upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer describes people of the best social standing, the elite or upper crust.

clue.text: Brisk movement of small singer backing Australia

indicators.note: going backwards means the word for the country is read from its end

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Cher is a famous American singer
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A dancer's quick routine as a little singer supports an Australian act.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively, quick movement in a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Like a crocodile arranging a Nile trip?

indicators.note: arranging puts things into a new order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone planning an Egyptian river cruise is as cold-blooded as a crocodile.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nile is famous for its crocodiles, which makes the question mark fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodiles are reptiles, so anything reptilian has the qualities of one.

clue.text: I'm in enclosure with last bits of hot jalapeño pepper

indicators.note: being in an enclosure means sitting inside it
the final letters of each word are the only ones kept

blocks.note: a pen is an animal enclosure
taken as written
the last letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone shut in a pen with a fiery jalapeño pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot jalapeño' reads as the spicy pepper itself, but only the final letters of those two words are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimento is a mild red sweet pepper, often stuffed into olives.

clue.text: Alfresco exit?

blocks.note: first meaning: in the open air
second meaning, read as two words: a door leading out

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that the second reading splits the word into OUT DOOR, a way out.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor means in the open air, as alfresco dining is, and an out door is literally an exit.

clue.text: Disease of sheep that is found by ditch

blocks.note: to scrap something is to ditch it
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A sheep illness discovered beside a drainage ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' looks like a trench in a field, but it is the verb meaning discard.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a fatal degenerative brain illness that affects sheep and goats.

clue.text: Leo, for example, or a lady abroad

blocks.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: It sounds like a choice between a man named Leo and a woman overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leo' looks like a man's name, but here it is the star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married woman, the equivalent of a lady or Mrs.

clue.text: Spellbound artist with small part

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist
PT is the short form of part

explanation.surface: A painter captivated while playing a minor role.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rapt is completely absorbed or enchanted, as if under a spell.

clue.text: This bread is mine, thank you

blocks.note: a pit is a coal mine
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone claims a loaf as their own and says thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive, but it is the noun for a colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, hollow Middle Eastern bread often filled with salad or meat.

clue.text: Lack of progress in country where women are excluded?

blocks.note: first meaning: a standstill
second meaning, read as two words: a nation run like a men-only party

explanation.surface: A nation that bars women stalls and fails to develop.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is a men-only celebration before a wedding, so the answer split as STAG NATION is a country without women.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a state of no growth or development, like still water that does not flow.

clue.text: In autumn it requires gunpowder ingredient

indicators.note: the answer lies in the words that follow, sitting within their letters

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word across the next two

explanation.surface: Come autumn, someone needs explosives, perhaps for Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, or saltpetre, is potassium nitrate, a key component of black powder.

clue.text: Month not the first that may be triumphal

indicators.note: not keeping the first means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a month of the year

explanation.surface: A month that marks a triumph, though not the opening one of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'triumphal' suggests a victory march, but it describes a monument.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumphal arch is a monumental gateway built to celebrate a victory, like the Arc de Triomphe.

clue.text: Game of pool

blocks.note: surface reading: a round of the cue-and-balls table game
setter's reading: a ball game played in a swimming pool

explanation.walkthrough: Pool suggests the bar-room table game; the sport meant is played by swimmers in a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a team ball sport played by swimmers in a swimming bath, scoring in floating nets.

clue.text: Fool turning to dot a couple of i's

indicators.note: turning around makes the little word run backwards
dotting places a mark among the letters, here set between the pair

blocks.note: two of the letter I
D stands for the dot itself, placed between the two letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dimwit dutifully turning to the job of dotting his i's.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'to', then D dotted between two I's, read backwards gives IDIOT; the IDI part reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, a synonym for fool.

clue.text: Come to Korea — Chinese part

indicators.note: only a portion of the neighbouring words is taken, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: An invitation to visit Korea, the Chinese portion of the trip included.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to arrive at it, so it is a synonym for come to.

clue.text: Rambling rose with sedan — what driver needs?

indicators.note: a rambling plant sprawls in every direction, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: the letters of both words, joined by with

explanation.surface: A climbing rose sprawls over a parked saloon car, bothering its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling rose' is a real garden plant, so Rambling looks like part of its name; a sedan is a saloon car.
explanation.definitionFit: Road sense is the instinct for traffic and hazards that every motorist must have.
